messages:
mike_h: Quick RFC follow-up — we shipped the canary gating prototype last week. Wanted to sync on automatic fallback rules before we bake this into Dedicated and Private configs.
ana_r: SG, what's the ask?
mike_h: Two things: 1) policy surface — what knobs do we expose to customers vs keep internal, 2) automatic fallback decision logic (when to route to fallback variant vs rollback).
xia_w: +1. My concern is exposing too many levers. Customers will misconfigure thresholds and trigger noisy rollbacks. Suggest sane defaults and an opt-in advanced policy.
samir: Agreed. Defaults should be: p95 latency increase >20% for 2 consecutive minutes OR error rate spike >1% above baseline -> trigger fallback. Keep cooldown 5m.
ana_r: Can we add quality regression check? e.g., eval-set spike in perplexity or rerank MRR drop. That requires storage of rolling evaluation results.
mike_h: Yes, quality is important but expensive to compute. Proposal: lightweight approximation — sample 1% of requests for eval against golden prompts and track a weighted score. Only allow quality-triggered fallback if combined with latency or error signal (avoid false positives).
deploy-bot: Canary rollout: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%, automated checks at each step. Abort on failing check.
xia_w: About fallbacks: prefer routing to a compatible model variant (e.g., quantized FP16 -> FP32 stable variant), not straight rollback of the whole rollout, so load stays up. Need to ensure KV cache compatibility across variants.
samir: KV cache compatibility is tricky. If model architecture identical, we can share cache; otherwise warm caches on fallback nodes by shadowing traffic for a short window. Shadowing config must not affect billing.
ana_r: Operational concerns: tracing must tag requests with rollout id and selected variant. Metrics pipeline needs per-variant p95, errors, and quality_score. Also expose a per-route "fallback_count" metric.
mike_h: Good. Sketch of a policy object we can store in control plane (yaml):
```yaml
policy_name: default_canary
steps:
  - pct: 2
    checks: [latency_p95 < baseline*1.2, error_rate < baseline+0.01]
  - pct: 10
    checks: [latency_p95 < baseline*1.15, error_rate < baseline+0.005]
fallback_rules:
  - condition: latency_p95 > baseline*1.2 OR error_rate > baseline+0.01
    action: route_to_variant(quantized-safe)
    cooldown: 300 # seconds
    max_attempts: 3
```
xia_w: That looks reasonable. The control plane should also allow an "auto-rollback": boolean, default false for Private tenants. For Hosted we can set true.
samir: For automatic decisions, we need a small rules engine in the runtime that evaluates signals with short TTLs. Runtime should emit a compact event when it flips to fallback so Console can show the history.
ops-bot: Note: tie this to existing circuit-breaker infra. If a model variant starts failing across >X nodes, the CB will trip and fallback route is used.
ana_r: One more thing: user-visible implication. We need to annotate responses that were served by a fallback variant (headers or response metadata) for downstream debugging and A/B analysis.
mike_h: Action items: 1) ana/qa to propose lightweight eval set and sampling plan (ana), 2) xia to document KV cache compatibility and shadowing API, 3) samir to prototype runtime rules engine and event emission, 4) product to decide default auto-rollback policy for Hosted vs Private.
ana_r: I'll take (1). Plan to draft sampling doc by EOD Friday.
xia_w: I'll sketch compatibility matrix and shadowing implementation next week.
samir: I'll drop a PoC in the eng-platform repo with the rules evaluator and a small e2e test harness.
mike_h: Thanks. If no objections, I'll update the RFC with these decisions and add the policy YAML example.
xia_w: No objections from me. :thumbsup:
ana_r: approved.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary-gating-v2 -> stg at 2024-11-02T15:20:00Z
mike_h: Great. Leaving this thread open for any late concerns.
